note: Browser end-to-end observations from this run. Trusted input means CDP Input.dispatchKeyEvent / Input.dispatchMouseEvent sent through Kimi WebBridge; these go through the browser's real input pipeline and can obtain native pointer lock. The debug API (?debug) was used only for setup: teleport, fixed camera, stationary dummy targets, freezing bots, and reading state. Damage and scores came from the normal fire, match and simulation code.
viewport: 1440x900 CSS px, DPR 1, set with Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride (960x600 @ DSF 1.5, which compensates for the browser's 0.667 zoom)

checks.steps: Trusted click on 开始游戏, then 5 cycles of document.exitPointerLock() followed by a trusted click on 继续游戏
checks.observed: Every cycle returned to state playing with lock true; position and ammo did not drift

checks.steps: A CDP Escape key press while locked
checks.observed: Did not release native pointer lock (the browser reserves Esc for this; synthetic key events do not trigger it). Unlock was driven by exitPointerLock(), which follows the same pointerlockchange path to pause

Chrome rejected the lock request and the in-game message 浏览器拒绝了鼠标锁定… was shown with the game paused. After Page.bringToFront the same sequence locked on every attempt. Recorded as an environment/focus effect with correct fail-safe handling
